channel.title: Comp Science on [1697, 20747]
channel.description: Recent content in Comp Science on [1697, 20747]

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 6: The Bank of England Data Tape
item.description: How the model generates the Bank of England loan-level data tape, the testing regime that runs before and after the file is written, and why every rule is data, so the software can follow the Bank's template when it changes.

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 5: Credit Enhancement, Mechanism and Design
item.description: How the model sizes credit enhancement: the credit model, the scenario grid, the cash-flow waterfall, bisection, the sensitivity cushion, the swap and reserve design, and the checks against public deals.

item.title: Teaching YOLO Your Own Objects
item.description: Fourth post in the Luckfox build log: a short guide to training YOLOv8n on just your own objects and images, instead of the 80 everyday classes it ships with, and getting the result onto the RV1106's NPU.

item.title: Thirty Frames on One Core
item.description: Third post in the Luckfox build log. The detection board's CPU was spending most of its time recolouring pixels. Moving that work onto the chip's 2D engine, and showing every camera frame instead of only detected ones, took the live video from 16 to 30 frames a second.

item.title: Never Stop the Camera
item.description: Second post in the Luckfox build log. The detection board kept hanging, so the fix had to rest on evidence: crash logs that survive a reset, register dumps from the moment of failure, and A/B tests by the hundred.

item.title: The Vendor Stack Was the Fix
item.description: First post in the Luckfox build log. A Luckfox Pico Ultra (Rockchip RV1106) detection board got a web UI, then a whole new operating system -- because every hard problem it had come down to running Rockchip's parts outside Rockchip's stack.

item.title: No Two Banks Say It the Same Way
item.description: The last ten banks through the verification pipeline, read log by log. Why pre-coded Python scraping failed, why checking every cell by hand is not feasible, what it costs in tokens to get a bank through the QA gate, and how the agent's harness evolves session by session. Agents are the only viable path to a curated credit metric database at scale, and without that data a peer credit comparison ranks definitions, not banks.

item.title: How Neural Networks Learn to Tell a Cat From a Dog
item.description: The same 25,000 Kaggle cat and dog photos, four ways: a scikit-learn neural network, the identical network in PyTorch, a small convolutional network, and a pretrained YOLOv8 -- every number from code you can run.

item.title: Expensive On Purpose
item.description: Verifying one bank's worth of metrics against real source documents cost about half a million tokens. A more efficient reading method barely moved that number. Here's why the cost is the point, not a bug — and why it might belong on a local model instead of a metered API.

item.title: The Mouse Was Never Required
item.description: Driving Blender with text and voice through the Model Context Protocol, and what that means for anyone who finds a mouse the hardest part of CAD.

item.title: Not Every Pixel Needs an Answer
item.description: Tenth post in the APEX build log. Today: a real stereo depth pipeline finally produced correct numbers on real hardware, then turned out to run at a thirtieth of the camera's own frame rate -- and the fix wasn't faster hardware, it was asking for less.

item.title: Locked In, Never Measured
item.description: Ninth post in the APEX build log. Today: a stereo-vision detector's model choice, picked months ago and called 'locked in' ever since, finally got a stopwatch put on it -- and the number that came back reversed the choice.

item.title: Fast, But Undecoded
item.description: Eighth post in the APEX build log. Today: the AI HAT+ ran the newest YOLO generation at real speed and zero CPU load, then handed back nothing usable — because nobody had written the decode step for it yet.

item.title: What the Arduino Was Actually Doing
item.description: Seventh post in the APEX build log. Today: a wheel encoder, a return-to-base feature that now has three progressively-less-trusted ways to find its way home, and a reference design that turned out to be doing more than it looked like.

item.title: Same Shape, Different Paper
item.description: Sixth post in the APEX build log. Today: drawing the current ROS 2 architecture as an actual diagram after a paper published the same month turned out to describe the same shape on the same class of hardware -- then walking that one graph through two different operating modes to see what object avoidance actually means in each.

item.title: The Later That Came Early
item.description: Fifth post in the APEX build log (formerly APEX-DC). Today: the whole software stack moves off DonkeyCar and onto ROS 2 -- earlier than planned -- and why the swap was cheap because of a decision made months ago.

item.title: Stay On, Then Smooth, Then Fast
item.description: Fourth post in a build log for APEX-DC, an autonomous RC vehicle project. Today: reshaping the reinforcement-learning reward so staying on the track always outranks driving smoothly or driving fast, and a look ahead at where the software might go next.

item.title: From Static Overlay to Object Oriented Widget HUD
item.description: Third post in the APEX-DC build log. Today: the on-screen instrument HUD stopped being one 1,000-line file and became a package of independent widgets bound to a grid — and why that made a two-line fix out of what would have been a rewrite.

item.title: The Tilde Is the Point
item.description: Second post in the APEX-DC build log. Today: a distance estimate for the one camera that can't actually measure distance — and why the number is printed with a tilde in front of it.

item.title: Radar Without Range
item.description: First post in a build log for APEX-DC, an autonomous RC vehicle project. Today: turning a single-camera live stream into a dashboard with two HUD-overlay feeds, a live object table, and two top-down maps — one of them deliberately not to scale.

item.title: Audit the Neighbor Too
item.description: A metric in active use across 34 banks had never been formally checked. Auditing it properly caught five real bugs. Cross-checking it against the metric next door caught four more, for free.

item.title: Confirmed, Not Claimed
item.description: A field that says a fact is true and a fact that's actually been checked look identical, right up until they disagree. Why file identity now lives in a separate, independently-built register instead of a column on the record it describes.

item.title: Whose Bank Is This?
item.description: Group and subsidiary are both real, both rated, and easy to conflate. Why this project scopes to group-consolidated only, deliberately, with the architecture already built for the alternative it isn't doing yet.

item.title: Post PDF
item.description: A placeholder for the point this whole project is quietly waiting for: machine-readable regulatory disclosure making most of the ingestion layer unnecessary.

item.title: Antidote for Large Liar Model
item.description: Why the ingestion pipeline was designed, from the first line of code, so the LLM writing phase can never become the source of a fact — and what error handling actually means when the failure mode is confident invention, not a crash.

item.title: Not a Specification
item.description: The brief was 'write a bank's credit paper.' That's aspiration, not a specification. This is the outline of what the real problem turned out to be, and the path it set.

item.title: Adding the 61st Bank
item.description: How this project's bank-ingestion pipeline has changed since May, what Claude Code actually does in it now, and what happens end to end when a new bank gets added.

item.title: One Metric, Three Rulebooks
item.description: Why a Stage 3 ratio can't exist on a US bank's balance sheet, and what to do architecturally once you notice a whole class of bug shaped like that.

item.title: LLM Credit Paper Generator
item.description: Building a domain-grounded AI bank credit analyst — what worked, what didn't, and why fine-tuning was not the answer.

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 4: Outputs, Assumptions and Limits
item.description: What the model produces (BoE tape, investor report, pitch deck, draft prospectus), what is still a placeholder, and the limits of a public-data build.

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 3: Building the Deal
item.description: From warehouse to tranched deal: pool selection, the frozen static set, rating stresses, capital-stack sizing, a sensitivity cushion, challengers and issuance economics.

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 2: The Parties and the Waterfall
item.description: Who does what in a UK RMBS, and how the cash moves through the revenue and principal waterfalls every month.

item.title: Securitisation 101 — Part 1: What It Is, and Why the Data Comes First
item.description: What securitisation is, how a UK RMBS is generated end to end from a warehouse of loans, and a worked sample deal.

item.title: Tree CLI
item.description: Quick reminder/overview on tree CLI tool.
